title: SDK handoff: microteaching sprintplay journal
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook for a short, pragmatic microteaching sprint we can run to hand off the SDK (js/py + CLI) to integrator teams and internal partners. The emphasis is: teach production patterns, expose common failure modes, capture reproducible smoke tests, and leave a one-page quickstart that non-engineers can follow.

Rationale / constraints:
- We have many long-form docs; adoption stalls because teams need quick wins and concrete exercises.
- Microteaching = short instructor-led sessions (10–20m) + immediate lab task (15–30m).
- Sprint run length: 3 half-days (can be condensed to a single day depending on partner availability).
- Audience: internal Platform teams, Customer Solutions, and early pilot customers (engineers + one PM per pod).

Outcomes we want by sprint end:
1) Each pod ships a trivial integration that calls Redwood API via SDK (token handling, streaming response) and is observable.
2) They run and pass a minimal smoke-suite: auth, stream fallback, rate-limit handling, basic latency telemetry.
3) One signed-off quickstart (single page) per pod capturing any local gotchas.
4) List of immediate docs/code fixes prioritized for next sprint.

Sprint agenda (3 half-days / flexible):
- Day 0 (prep): instructor checklist, sandboxes, tokens, sample repo forks seeded
- Day 1 (half-day): Foundations + Local Loop
  - 10m: Ten-minute framing: "What winning integration looks like"
  - 20m: API model: requests, streams, embeddings, error surface
  - 15m: Live: install SDK, set token env, run hello-world (streaming chat)
  - 30m: Lab #1: wire a tiny HTTP endpoint that proxies a chat call (validate headers, CORS note)
  - 15m: Debrief + capture "first pain" notes
- Day 2 (half-day): Robustness & Observability
  - 15m: Failure modes map (401s, 429s, partial streams, KV cache misses)
  - 20m: Telemetry: what we instrument (latency p95/p99, token consumption, route, model)
  - 30m: Live: add lightweight telemetry/metrics to the sample app (console + basic prometheus client)
  - 40m: Lab #2: simulate rate limit, fallback to smaller model variant, confirm graceful degradation
  - 15m: Capture data points for console dashboards (what useful drilldowns look like)
- Day 3 (half-day): Delivery + Quickstart drafting
  - 10m: Quick checklist: security review, KMS notes, secrets rotation
  - 30m: Lab #3: produce a one-pager quickstart with copy/paste commands, runbook for first incident
  - 30m: Handoff ritual: where to open tickets, PR style guide for SDK adaptations, sample telemetry alerts
  - 20m: Retro + commit next actions

Lab exercises (deliverables per pod):
- Lab #1 deliverable: running sample proxy that does a streaming chat and writes the final assistant text to a file. (Must include README with run steps).
- Lab #2 deliverable: test harness that triggers 429 behavior and shows fallback to a lower-cost model; includes a short script to replay the incident.
- Lab #3 deliverable: single-page quickstart + three screenshots (console metric view, sample logs, request/response snippet).

Instructor checklist (prep):
- Seed forked sample repos with branch 'microteach/{pod-name}' (one branch per pod).
- Create ephemeral API tokens scoped to sandbox orgs; ensure CORS allowed for sample web proxy domain.
- Pre-wire a simple prometheus export on sample app and a dashboard template in Console.
- Smoke-suite: three curl-based tests (auth, streaming fallback, rate limit simulation).
- Slack channel + calendar invites + retrospective doc link.

Quickstart one-pager template (what to include):
- Title + 30s blurb describing purpose
- Prereqs: node 18+/python3.10+, token in env, git clone command
- Commands: install, env export, run dev, run smoke tests (exact curl commands)
- Troubleshooting section: common errors and first checks (token, network, region mismatch)
- Next steps + where to ask for help (Slack channel, doc links)

Telemetry & gate metrics to capture during labs:
- Request/response latency p50/p95/p99 (by route)
- Tokens consumed per request (histogram)
- Model variant used and fallback counts
- Error rates by class (4xx vs 5xx)
- Rolling 5-minute alert threshold examples (error rate > 2% or stream-stalls > 0.5%)

Minimal smoke tests (curl snippets to include in repo README):
- Auth test: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
- Stream test: quick curl POST to /chat with streaming accept header and pipe output to jq to assert 'assistant' field present
- Rate-limit sim: replay a 100-request loop at 200ms interval and ensure fallback kicks in (script included)

Known open questions / risks (to capture in retro):
- How should we present quantization/precision tradeoffs to integrators? Short note vs deeper workshop?
- SDK CLI: should we add an ‘init’ that scaffolds telemetry and quickstart automatically? Scope/time?
- Sandbox token churn: need a simple revocation flow for tokens issued per-sprint.
- Non-engineer participants: can we prepare a "reader mode" quickstart that removes code steps and focuses on runbook + contract checks?

Immediate followups (owner + eta):
- Priya: seed sample repos and create sandbox tokens (ETA 2025-01-16)
- Liam: prepare console dashboard template + share snapshot (ETA 2025-01-18)
- Ava: draft one-page quickstart template and circulate (ETA 2025-01-15)
- Diego: write smoke-suite scripts and add to sample repo (ETA 2025-01-17)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep labs low-friction: default sample uses small model so costs negligible.
- Encourage teams to commit a single quickstart PR before sprint ends — that's the acceptance criteria.
- Capture every unique local error path participants hit and add to FAQ; this is gold for reducing friction.

Appendix: one-line runbook for first incident
1) Collect request id + timestamp from participant logs
2) Check Console for recent error spikes and model fallbacks
3) If 401: verify token and org scope, rotate if compromised
4) If 429: confirm autoscaling / dedicated capacity policy; if transient, instruct retry-after-based backoff
5) If partial stream: run local repro with --stream-debug and escalate to runtime team with attached logs

(End of working notes)
